walkthroughs.body_html:
Working as a Physicist — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Working as a Physicist brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Working as a Physicist.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A car travels 4 km north then 3 km east. What is its displacement magnitude?
options: 7 km
5 km
1 km
25 km

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
options: Acceleration
Momentum
Kinetic energy
Weight

mcqs.q: What condition must be met for total internal reflection to occur?
options: Light must go from a less dense to a denser medium.
Light must travel from a denser to a less dense medium AND strike the boundary at an angle greater than the critical angle.
The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.
Any angle is fine as long as the light is going into a less dense medium.

mcqs.q: When you push a wall, what does Newton's third law say about the wall?
options: The wall only pushes back if your force is strong enough to make it react.
The wall exerts an equal and opposite force on you at the same instant.
The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.
Light must go from a less dense to a denser medium.

mcqs.q: How does the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depend on light intensity?
options: It does not — max KE depends only on the frequency of the light; intensity affects the rate (number) of electrons emitted.
The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.
Higher intensity gives photoelectrons more kinetic energy.
Intensity has no effect on anything in the photoelectric effect.
